title.zh: Agent 又慢又贵时，为什么“换小模型”通常不是答案？
title.en: When an Agent Is Slow and Expensive, Why Isn’t “Use a Smaller Model” the Answer?

dek.zh: 用端到端 SLO、error budget、tail latency、单位经济、risk-weighted routing、load shedding 与可验证降级收束可靠性设计。
dek.en: Complete the reliability design with end-to-end SLOs, error budgets, tail latency, unit economics, risk-weighted routing, load shedding, and verifiable degradation.

html.zh:
Agent 的 latency 和 cost 不是一个模型调用的属性。一次任务可能包含多轮 prefill/decode、retrieval、并行 tools、重试、approval wait、sandbox cold start、artifact verification 和 repair。把主模型换小可能降低单次 token 成本，却增加 tool selection error、repair turns 和人工 review，最终每个成功任务更贵、更慢。反过来，使用最强模型处理所有步骤也会浪费低风险结构化工作。

可靠控制面应先定义 task-class contract：在给定风险与质量门槛下，任务在多久内进入可验证终态、允许花多少 token/tool/compute、人类介入率多高、哪些安全门永不降级。Admission 估算需求和可用 budget；router 选择 model/tool/sandbox/concurrency；runtime 根据队列和 error budget 限流、重试或降级；terminal verifier 只为满足 claims 的结果记 success。

核心判断：优化目标不是 cost/request 或 average latency，而是满足安全与质量约束的 cost per verified outcome，以及 terminal latency 的尾部。无法在预算内可靠完成的任务应排队、拆分、升级或拒绝，而不是静默降低正确性。
html.en:
Agent latency and cost are not properties of one model call. A task may include repeated prefill and decode, retrieval, parallel tools, retries, approval wait, sandbox cold start, artifact verification, and repair. Replacing the main model with a smaller one may reduce token price while increasing tool-selection errors, repair turns, and human review, making each successful task slower and more expensive. Using the strongest model for every step wastes simple, low-risk structured work.

A reliable control plane first defines a task-class contract. Given risk and quality gates, how quickly must the task reach a verifiable terminal state? What token, tool, compute, and human-intervention budgets apply? Which safety gates never degrade? Admission estimates demand and available budget. Routing chooses model, tool, sandbox, and concurrency. Runtime limits, retries, or degrades according to queues and error budgets. The terminal verifier counts success only when claims pass.

Core judgment: optimize neither cost per request nor average latency. Optimize cost per verified outcome under safety and quality constraints, plus the tail of terminal latency. A task that cannot complete reliably within budget should queue, split, escalate, or reject rather than silently lower correctness.

title.zh: 把 Trace、Authorization 与 Sandbox 变成可运营 contract
title.en: Turn trace, authorization, and sandboxing into an operable contract

html.zh:
1/4 给出 evidence graph，可精确分解 model/tool/observer/verifier 的时间与成本；2/4 确立授权和 taint gate 不可被模型绕过；3/4 将 sandbox tier、broker 和 teardown 纳入 lifecycle。今天这些数据成为 routing/admission 的输入。没有 trace identity 的 cost 账单无法归因到 task；没有 verifier 的 success denominator 会把“生成了答案”当完成；没有风险标签的降级策略会优先牺牲安全。

例如代码修复任务可分：轻量模型分类/定位，强模型设计 patch，sandbox 运行 tests，observer 验证 artifact。若强模型不可用，可以延迟设计步骤，不能让轻量模型直接在 production checkout 写入；若 verifier 不可用，可以完成计算但停在 verification_pending，不能为了 SLO 将其记成功。

因此 reliability policy 是多维 contract，而不是一个 timeout。它声明 required claims、deadline、priority、max cost、retry/repair budget、allowed routes、degradable features、human escalation 和 fail-open/fail-closed。每个 task 在开始前绑定 policy version，便于 replay 和比较。
html.en:
Part 1 produced an evidence graph that attributes model, tool, observer, and verifier time and cost. Part 2 established authorization and taint gates that models cannot bypass. Part 3 integrated sandbox tiers, brokers, and teardown into lifecycle. Today those signals feed routing and admission. Cost without trace identity cannot be attributed to a task. Success without a verifier counts “an answer was generated” as completion. Degradation without risk labels sacrifices safety first.

A code-repair task can use a small model for classification and localization, a stronger model for patch design, a sandbox for tests, and an observer for artifact verification. If the strong model is unavailable, delay design rather than allowing the small model to write directly into a production checkout. If the verifier is unavailable, computation may finish but state remains verification pending; it does not become SLO success.

Reliability policy is therefore a multidimensional contract, not one timeout. It declares required claims, deadline, priority, maximum cost, retry and repair budgets, allowed routes, degradable features, human escalation, and fail-open or fail-closed rules. Every task binds a policy version before execution for replay and comparison.

title.zh: 机制：从 admission 到 verified outcome 的控制回路
title.en: Mechanism: the control loop from admission to verified outcome

html.zh:
1. 定义 task classes

按 intent/risk/effect/quality 建类：只读问答、内部草稿、代码修改、外部消息、财务/权限变更等。每类绑定 required claims、quality evaluator、terminal deadline、cost ceiling、allowed models/tools/sandbox、approval 和 retention。不要用一个全局 SLO 混合不同损失函数。

2. 端到端 SLI

从 acceptedAt 到 terminal verdict 测 terminal latency，另拆 queue、model prefill/decode、retrieval、tool、sandbox, approval wait、observer/verifier、repair。Success 仅为 required claims pass 且无 unresolved effect；unknown/manual review 单列。Cost 绑定 workflowId，累计 tokens、model price、tool/API、compute、storage、egress 和 human minutes。

3. Admission control

任务到达时估算 token/steps/tools/sandbox/observer 和 worst-case retry budget，检查 tenant/user/global concurrency、queue age、deadline feasibility、cost/risk budget。不可行则 reject、schedule、ask to narrow 或 route human，而不是接受后超时。Admission reservation 防止大量长任务挤掉短高优任务。

4. Risk-weighted routing

Router 使用 task features、required capabilities、data sensitivity、historical model/tool eval、current latency/cost/availability。简单 deterministic step 用 code/tool，不用 LLM；低风险 classification 用小模型；复杂 planning 用强模型；高风险 action 除模型质量外要求 verifier/approval/sandbox tier。Route snapshot 进入 trace。

5. Budget decomposition

总 deadline 分给 planning、calls、tools、verification 和 reserve；总 cost 分给 base attempt、retry、repair、observer 和 human。Child budgets 不能超过 parent，且保留 cancellation/cleanup 时间。模型输出 token cap、context budget、tool result size、并行 fan-out 和 retry attempts 都是显式配额。

6. Tail latency 与 hedging

关注 p95/p99 terminal latency，而非平均。并行 tool fan-out 的 completion 受最慢 child 影响。只读、幂等且高 variance 操作可在阈值后发 hedged request，首个有效结果获胜，取消其他；副作用 write 不随意 hedge。Hedging 使用全局 extra-work budget，避免负载高时放大拥塞。

7. Retry/repair owner

一个层负责 transport retry；workflow 负责 semantic repair。retry 仅限明确 transient 且 idempotent/reconciled；repair 依据 verifier failures 修改 plan。累计 retry+repair cost/latency 计入 task budget，超过后 manual review/fail。成功后重试的 late result 去重。

8. Degradation ladder

预先标记 mandatory 与 optional：可降 example count、retrieval breadth、parallel speculative branches、解释长度、非关键 observer frequency；不可降 authorization、tenant isolation、idempotency、required verifier、data classification。每级 degradation 有 quality delta eval 和 user-visible status，不能临时“先跳过验证”。

9. Load shedding 与 fairness

队列按 tenant/priority/risk 做 weighted fair scheduling；限制 per-tenant in-flight、token rate、tool rate 和 sandbox slots。过载先拒绝低优/可重试任务或返回 retry-after，再缩 optional work；保护 control-plane observers/verifiers/cleanup 容量。不能让批量后台 Agent 饿死交互请求。

10. Error budget policy

SLO 允许的 bad outcomes 构成 error budget，按 task class 计算。Burn rate 超阈值时冻结高风险 feature rollout、收窄 routes、提高 verifier sampling、降低 concurrency 或切回 known-good snapshot。安全 violation（cross-tenant、unauthorized effect、secret egress）是独立 zero-tolerance gate，不与普通 availability budget 互换。

11. Release/canary

新 model/prompt/tool/schema/router 先 offline replay/counterfactual，再 shadow，再 stratified canary。比较 verified success、tail terminal latency、cost/outcome、repair/human rate、safety gates。Sequential tests/guardrails 避免小样本过早放量；rollback pin prompt/model/catalog/policy snapshots，并处理 in-flight runs。

12. Cost attribution 与优化

成本按 successful/verified task、task class、tenant、route 与 stage 聚合。区分 productive tokens 与 discarded/repair tokens，cache hit、unused retrieval、duplicate tools、failed sandbox startup、observer overhead。优化从最大 waste pool 下手，并以 quality/risk guardrail 复验；不以单价最低替代总效用。

13. Verifiable degradation/recovery

每个 degraded outcome 带 policy version、skipped optional claims、remaining limitations、cost/latency evidence。依赖恢复后新 tasks 回升前先 canary，旧 tasks 不静默改变 route。若 verifier unavailable，状态是 waiting/unknown，不是 success；若 budget exhausted，明确 partial result 或 fail。
html.en:
1. Define task classes

Classify by intent, risk, effect, and quality: read-only answers, internal drafts, code changes, external messages, financial or permission changes, and so on. Each class binds required claims, quality evaluator, terminal deadline, cost ceiling, allowed models, tools, and sandbox, approval, and retention. Do not mix different loss functions into one global SLO.

2. Define end-to-end SLIs

Measure terminal latency from acceptedAt to terminal verdict, then decompose queue, model prefill and decode, retrieval, tools, sandbox, approval wait, observer and verifier, and repair. Success means required claims pass and no effect remains unresolved. Unknown and manual review are separate. Cost attaches to workflow ID and includes tokens, model pricing, tool and API fees, compute, storage, egress, and human minutes.

3. Control admission

At arrival, estimate tokens, steps, tools, sandbox, observer, and worst-case retry budget. Check tenant, user, and global concurrency, queue age, deadline feasibility, and cost and risk budgets. If infeasible, reject, schedule, ask to narrow scope, or route to a human rather than accepting and timing out. Reservations prevent many long tasks from starving short high-priority work.

4. Route by risk and evidence

The router uses task features, required capabilities, data sensitivity, historical model and tool evaluations, and current latency, cost, and availability. Deterministic steps use code or tools instead of an LLM. Low-risk classification uses a small model; difficult planning uses a stronger one. High-risk action also requires verifier, approval, and sandbox tier. The route snapshot enters the trace.

5. Decompose budgets

Divide total deadline among planning, calls, tools, verification, and reserve. Divide total cost among base attempt, retries, repair, observers, and human review. Child budgets never exceed parents and preserve cancellation and cleanup time. Output token caps, context budget, tool-result size, parallel fan-out, and retry attempts are explicit quotas.

6. Manage tail latency and hedging

Track p95 and p99 terminal latency, not only averages. Parallel tool fan-out completes at the slowest child. Read-only, idempotent, high-variance operations may launch a hedged request after a threshold; the first valid result wins and others cancel. Side-effecting writes are not casually hedged. Hedging consumes a global extra-work budget so overload does not amplify itself.

7. Assign one retry and repair owner

One layer owns transport retries; the workflow owns semantic repair. Retry only explicit transient classes with idempotency or reconciliation. Repair changes the plan according to verifier failure. Cumulative retry and repair latency and cost count against the task budget. Exceeding it moves to manual review or failure. Late successful results deduplicate.

8. Predefine a degradation ladder

Mark work mandatory or optional in advance. Degrade example count, retrieval breadth, speculative branches, explanation length, or non-critical observer frequency. Never degrade authorization, tenant isolation, idempotency, required verification, or data classification. Each level has an evaluated quality delta and user-visible status. “Skip verification for now” is not graceful degradation.

9. Shed load fairly

Use weighted fair scheduling by tenant, priority, and risk, with per-tenant in-flight, token-rate, tool-rate, and sandbox-slot limits. Under overload, reject low-priority retryable tasks or return retry-after before reducing optional work. Protect control-plane observer, verifier, and cleanup capacity. Batch background agents cannot starve interactive requests.

10. Apply an error-budget policy

Bad outcomes allowed by the SLO form an error budget per task class. High burn freezes risky feature rollout, narrows routes, increases verifier sampling, lowers concurrency, or returns to a known-good snapshot. Safety violations such as cross-tenant access, unauthorized effect, and secret egress remain independent zero-tolerance gates and cannot trade against availability budget.

11. Release through replay, shadow, and canary

A new model, prompt, tool, schema, or router passes offline replay and counterfactual evaluation, then shadow mode, then stratified canary. Compare verified success, terminal tail latency, cost per outcome, repair and human-review rates, and safety gates. Sequential guardrails prevent premature ramp on small samples. Rollback pins prompt, model, catalog, and policy snapshots and handles in-flight runs.

12. Attribute and optimize cost

Aggregate cost by verified task, task class, tenant, route, and stage. Separate productive tokens from discarded and repair tokens, cache hits, unused retrieval, duplicate tool calls, failed sandbox starts, and observer overhead. Optimize the largest waste pool and re-evaluate quality and risk. Lowest unit price does not imply best total utility.

13. Verify degradation and recovery

Every degraded outcome records policy version, skipped optional claims, remaining limitations, and cost and latency evidence. When a dependency recovers, canary new tasks before restoring routes; old tasks do not silently change route. An unavailable verifier yields waiting or unknown, not success. Budget exhaustion produces an explicit partial result or failure.

title.zh: 必要数学：SLO、队列、tail 与单位经济
title.en: Essential mathematics: SLOs, queues, tails, and unit economics

html.zh:
Error budget

目标周期内有 N 个 eligible tasks，SLO success target S，则允许 bad outcomes B=N·(1−S)。若窗口已消耗 b，burn fraction b/B 驱动 release policy。Eligible/成功定义必须版本化且以 verifier verdict 为准；改变 denominator 会伪造 budget。

Queue stability

到达率 λ、服务率 μ，基本稳定条件 ρ=λ/μ<1。ρ 接近 1 时 queue/tail latency 非线性上升；因此不能把平均 capacity 跑满。多类任务用 service demand 和 priority 估算，admission 留 headroom，hedging/retry 也计入 λ。

Cost per verified outcome

若总花费 C，verified successes V，则 CPVO=C/V。某 route 单次便宜但降低 success，会使 CPVO 上升。Route 选择可最大化 E[U]=P(success)·Value−Cost−RiskPenalty−LatencyPenalty，同时受 safety hard constraints；不是把所有维度任意加权后绕过安全。
html.en:
Error budget

With N eligible tasks in a target window and success objective S, allowed bad outcomes are B=N·(1−S). If b has been consumed, burn fraction b/B drives release policy. Eligibility and success definitions are versioned and based on verifier verdict. Changing the denominator manufactures budget.

Queue stability

For arrival rate λ and service rate μ, basic stability requires ρ=λ/μ<1. As ρ approaches one, queue and tail latency grow nonlinearly, so average capacity cannot run full. Multiple task classes use service demand and priority; admission preserves headroom, and hedging plus retry count toward λ.

Cost per verified outcome

For total spend C and verified successes V, CPVO=C/V. A cheaper attempt that reduces success can increase CPVO. Routing may maximize E[U]=P(success)·Value−Cost−RiskPenalty−LatencyPenalty subject to safety hard constraints. Weighted utility does not permit trading away safety.

title.zh: 对 Agent 系统的影响

html.zh:
能力：混合 model/tool/sandbox route 让复杂任务在必要处用强能力、简单处用确定性组件。Budget 让 Agent 能规划而不是无限探索。

可靠性：terminal verdict 统一 success denominator；unknown、partial、manual review 不被隐藏。Error budget 将线上 incident 与 feature velocity 连接，避免只看 demo quality。

安全：authorization、isolation、idempotency、required verification 是 hard gates，不进入 cost/latency degradation。高风险 route 即使更贵也保留；budget 不足时拒绝。

经济性：按 verified outcome 和 waste stage 计费揭示小模型 repair、重试放大、unused context、tool fan-out、observer overhead。FinOps 与 reliability 使用同一 workflow identity，不再对不上账。
html.en:
Capability: mixed model, tool, and sandbox routes use strong capabilities only where necessary and deterministic components for simple steps. Budgets let agents plan rather than explore without bound.

Reliability: terminal verdict creates one success denominator. Unknown, partial, and manual review are not hidden. Error budgets connect incidents to feature velocity rather than relying on demo quality.

Security: authorization, isolation, idempotency, and required verification are hard gates outside cost and latency degradation. High-risk routes retain safeguards even when expensive; insufficient budget causes rejection.

Economics: accounting per verified outcome and waste stage exposes small-model repairs, retry amplification, unused context, tool fan-out, and observer overhead. FinOps and reliability share workflow identity and reconcile.

html.zh:
• 平均 latency：隐藏 p99/approval/repair 尾部；测 terminal distribution 和 stage breakdown。
  • cost/request：忽略 success/repair/human；用 CPVO。
  • 过载时多 retry/hedge：放大 λ；全局 extra-work/retry budget。
  • 降级跳过 verifier：把未知记成功；required claims 不可降。
  • 全局 SLO：低风险量掩盖高风险失败；按 task/risk class 分层。
  • 小模型 everywhere：选择/repair 错误放大；按 stage eval route。
  • error budget 与安全互换：跨租户/越权被 availability 抵消；独立 zero-tolerance gates。
  • 恢复即全量回切：依赖抖动形成 thundering herd；canary/ramp、queue drain、hysteresis。
html.en:
• Average latency: hides p99, approval, and repair tails. Measure terminal distributions and stage breakdown.
  • Cost per request: ignores success, repair, and human work. Use cost per verified outcome.
  • Retry and hedge under overload: amplifies arrival rate. Use global extra-work and retry budgets.
  • Degrade by skipping verification: counts unknown as success. Required claims never degrade.
  • One global SLO: low-risk volume hides high-risk failure. Stratify by task and risk class.
  • Small model everywhere: selection and repair errors compound. Evaluate routes by stage.
  • Trade safety against error budget: cross-tenant or unauthorized effects disappear inside availability. Keep independent zero-tolerance gates.
  • Restore everything at once: dependency flapping creates a thundering herd. Canary, ramp, drain queues, and use hysteresis.

html.zh:
• 优化 cost per verified outcome 与 terminal tail latency，不是 request 单价或平均 latency。
  • task class contract 定义 quality/risk/deadline/cost/retry/route/degradation；开始时绑定版本。
  • admission 在接受前证明容量、deadline 和 budget 可行；过载时 load shed 而非无限排队。
  • degradation 只删除预先评测的 optional work；授权、隔离、幂等和 required verifier 永不降。
  • error budget 驱动 routing/release，安全 violation 是独立 gate；恢复需 canary 与 hysteresis。
html.en:
• Optimize cost per verified outcome and terminal tail latency, not request price or average latency.
  • A task-class contract defines quality, risk, deadline, cost, retry, route, and degradation and binds a version at start.
  • Admission proves capacity, deadline, and budget feasibility before acceptance; overload sheds load rather than queueing forever.
  • Degradation removes only evaluated optional work. Authorization, isolation, idempotency, and required verification never degrade.
  • Error budgets govern routing and releases, while safety violations are independent gates. Recovery uses canary and hysteresis.

html.zh:
• Google SRE: Service Level Objectives — SLI/SLO 设计与用户导向可靠性。
  • Google SRE Workbook: Error Budget Policy — error budget 与 release policy 示例。
  • Google SRE: Handling Overload — load shedding、capacity 与过载处理。
  • Dean & Barroso, The Tail at Scale — tail latency、hedged requests 等技术论文。
  • AWS Builders' Library: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter — retry amplification、backoff、jitter、token bucket。
  • FinOps Unit Economics — unit economics 与业务价值归因框架。
  • NIST AI RMF — AI risk governance、measurement 与 management。

task-class contract、CPVO、risk-weighted routing、degradation ladder 与 verified recovery 是本文基于这些 SRE/FinOps 原则的编辑性综合。
html.en:
• Google SRE: Service Level Objectives — user-oriented SLI and SLO design.
  • Google SRE Workbook: Error Budget Policy — an example linking error budgets and release policy.
  • Google SRE: Handling Overload — load shedding, capacity, and overload handling.
  • Dean and Barroso, The Tail at Scale — a paper on tail latency and techniques including hedged requests.
  • AWS Builders' Library: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter — retry amplification, backoff, jitter, and token buckets.
  • FinOps Unit Economics — a framework for unit economics and business-value attribution.
  • NIST AI RMF — AI-risk governance, measurement, and management.

The task-class contract, cost per verified outcome, risk-weighted routing, degradation ladder, and verified recovery are editorial synthesis from these SRE and FinOps principles.

title.zh: 本系列收束与下一条主线

html.zh:
今天已完成：task-class SLO 统一 verified quality、terminal tail latency、cost 与 safety；admission/routing/budget/retry/degradation/load shedding/error budget/release gate 形成闭环。Required safety/verification 永不降级，budget 不足时明确排队、部分结果或拒绝。

四篇合起来：trace/evidence 提供可验证 truth；prompt injection 通过外部 authorization 隔离；sandbox/brokers 控制 code/computer use；SLO/error budget/economics 将能力、风险、尾延迟和成本变成可运营 policy。

本系列状态：Reliability 与 Safety 内核 4/4 已完成。下一条系统主线进入 Advanced Systems，从 multi-agent coordination 的 shared-state、delegation、ownership 与 conflict 开始，再进入 model routing、research/computer-use architectures 与 self-improvement 边界。
html.en:
Completed today: task-class SLOs unify verified quality, terminal tail latency, cost, and safety. Admission, routing, budgets, retries, degradation, load shedding, error budgets, and release gates form a control loop. Required safety and verification never degrade; insufficient budget yields explicit queueing, partial result, or rejection.

Across four parts: traces and evidence provide verifiable truth; prompt injection is contained through external authorization; sandboxes and brokers constrain code and computer use; SLOs, error budgets, and economics turn capability, risk, tail latency, and cost into operable policy.

Series status: Reliability and Safety Internals 4/4 is complete. The next systematic track is Advanced Systems, beginning with shared state, delegation, ownership, and conflict in multi-agent coordination, then moving into model routing, research and computer-use architectures, and boundaries of self-improvement.
